If you cannot distinguish queued from computing, SAY SO on the surface. *** READER TRAPS THIS SURFACE MUST NOT REPEAT: updated_at in the /api/runs LIST IS NOT A LIVENESS SIGNAL (it read 68 min stale while the snapshot showed a round recorded 4.9 min earlier) - do not drive freshness from it; a FROZEN trajectory means a request is IN FLIGHT, not dead (one ran ~14 min and returned) so render it as a neutral fact; the Ollama GIN log writes ONLY ON COMPLETION so an in-flight request is invisible there; the GIN line is quoted and MULTI-SPACE so a naive grep matches nothing, and docker logs --since parses a bare timestamp as HOST LOCAL time; a cached 200 proves nothing - count arrivals, not status codes. *** HIGHEST VALUE ITEM: make the 80% disk threshold ALARM VISIBLY on /overview. Both the 2026-09-08 CT202 fill (hit 100%, killed the router an hour, destroyed 23 runs) and the 09-10 climb were SILENT on every operator surface.
